title: Quantile-aware admission to arrest long-tail suppression
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Multiple post-mortem investigations and live customer escalations in the last month revealed a recurring pattern: mixed-length workloads (short interactive requests + long-context generations) cause the continuous batcher admission policy to enter a hysteresis state where large in-flight long-context batches starve short requests. Symptoms include p95/p99 latency spikes for short requests, emergency tenant token throttling, and KV-cache churn leading to higher token cost and degraded quality for hosted, Dedicated and Private customers. This ticket designs and implements a quantile-aware admission controller plus a tenant shedder and aging-based reservations to restore fairness while bounding cost.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy a mixed-workload client that emits 80% short requests (~32 tokens) and 20% long-context requests (~8192 tokens) at sustained QPS on a single host pool.
2) Enable continuous batching with default admission heuristics.
3) Observe short-request p95 and p99 climb after sustained microbursts of long requests.
4) Trigger a second tenant with a burst of short requests; note preemption failures and increased cold-KV misses.
5) Record telemetry for batch sizes, admission rejections, KV cache evictions, and per-tenant queue depth.
investigation_notes:
- Root cause: admission uses an average-length signal that lags during bursts; long-context inflight reservations grow and block admission slices for latency-sensitive short flows.
- Contributing factor: eviction hysteresis in KV cache causes active prefetches for long sequences to displace shorter-sequence contexts.
- Observed eviction spikes correlate with increased token cost and error resurfacing for affected customers.
- Private deployments: upgrades with default admission exposed same regression when host-side config mirrored hosted defaults.
- Past mitigations (grace windows, prefetch quarantine) reduced but did not eliminate oscillations under prolonged mixed waves.
- Customer escalations tied to this include: Case RF-21 (LawFirmAI) and Case FIN-7 (payments vendor) where SLAs were missed; both reported 300x p99 worsening during nightly batch windows.
proposed_solution:
1) Quantile-aware admission engine: track recent request length distribution per ingress window (p50, p75, p90, p99) and compute admission budget using a weighted quantile target to limit inflight large-token reservations.
2) Age-based reservation decay: every reservation carries a timestamp and decays exponentially if not scheduled within Xms to prevent immortal reservations.
3) Tenant shedder: ephemeral soft-shed that reduces admission for tenants whose short-request latency exceeds threshold; shed decisions are reversible and rate-limited.
4) KV prefetch backoff policy: when eviction rate > threshold, suppress speculative prefetch for sequences above length L and prefer prefix/KV reuse.
5) Config knobs (server-side): quantile window size, decay half-life, shed thresholds, and per-tenant grace credits.
6) Metrics & guardrails: admission_rejections, inflight_tokens_by_length_bucket, kv_eviction_rate, short_request_p99, tenant_shed_events.
acceptance_criteria:
- Short-request p99 under mixed workload recovers to baseline within 2x original after 5 minutes of sustained mixed waves.
- No increase in 5xx errors for long-context generations after rollout beyond acceptable margin (+0.5%).
- KV eviction rate reduced by at least 30% during repro scenario.
- Feature toggle present to roll back to previous admission policy.
- Unit tests for admission decision logic and integration tests in the cluster-scale harness.
- Sign-offs from SRE and Product before gradual rollout.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1 (canary): enable quantile-aware admission on 5% of hosted capacity and a Dedicated test customer cluster for 24h, monitor defined metrics and run synthetic mixed workload.
Stage 2 (expand): if stable, expand to 25% over 6h and run closed-loop auto-safeguard to revert on p99 regression > 2x.
Stage 3 (private): provide opt-in config for Private customers and partner with Solutions to schedule low-risk upgrade windows.
Stage 4 (global): 100% rollout with telemetry retention baseline for 72h.
Emergency rollback: feature toggle + kill-switch on admission controller; immediate revert to average-length admission if shedding causes more harm.
test_plan:
- Unit: admission decision matrix unit tests for quantiles and tie-breaking.
- Integration: multi-host cluster test with synthetic clients reproducing mixed workload (short+long) and asserting p99 targets.
- Chaos: injector that simulates KV eviction spikes and host node drain to ensure aging prevents immortalized reservations.
- Customer mirror: run reproduction against a sanitized snapshot of LawFirmAI workload in staging.
- Load test: ramp to 3x production QPS to validate controller stability.

customer_escalations:
- LawFirmAI (RF-21): persistent short-request p99 spikes during 03:00-05:00 UTC batch window; threatened SLA credits.
- FinPayments (FIN-7): intermittent checkout latency for fraud model calls during mixed traffic.
Mitigation executed: temporary rate limits and manual tenant shielding while fix is developed for both Hosted and Dedicated. Private customers notified and given a workaround doc.
notes_for_oncall:
- How to toggle feature: /api/admin/feature/quantile_admission
- Emergency revert: set admission_mode=average_length on host group via infra tool.
- When to escalate: if short_request_p99 > 3x baseline for 30m and shed events > 5/min for a tenant, page Eng-oncall.
